cohorts.subjects: Living adult patients of Nigerian heritage (judged by one native Nigerian name) whose abdominal CT scans of 1 July 2017 to 30 June 2019 were taken from the radiology (CT) database of Lagoon Hospitals, Lagos, Nigeria; retrospective. Ethnic group: Yoruba 51%, Igbo 21%, the rest other or unknown tribes. Excluded: age below 18 or above 65, degenerative change at the bony landmarks, spondylolisthesis, signs of spondylodiscitis or other infection, images not clearly showing all lumbar vertebrae. Taken as representative of the normal population since not known to have lumbar symptoms. Numbers screened and excluded are not given.
cohorts.n_units: 120 abdominal CT scans, L1 to L5 each: 600 level measurements of each of APD and TD (Inference: one scan per patient; the paper counts 120 images and 120 observations and does not say whether any patient had two scans)

techniques.instrument: hospital CT workstation, sagittal and axial reconstructions side by side with linked reference lines, bone window, electronic cursor, values in mm
techniques.how: Canal anteroposterior diameter (APD) on the mid-sagittal cut, the cursor drawn perpendicular from the posterior border of each vertebral body back to the lamina, the midline position checked on the linked axial view at each level L1 to L5. The vertebral body AP diameter (VAPD) at the same level on the same cut, and the vertebral Torg ratio APD/VAPD; VAPD values themselves are not reported. Inference from Fig. 1: the lines sit at about mid-height of each body, not at the disc.
techniques.magnification: not a projection, so no film magnification; display zoomed to 4.00x on the workstation, measurements read in mm (Inference: the workstation's calibrated distance tool)
techniques.observers: not stated; only the researcher had access to the data (Inference: one observer, one reading, no reliability figures)

techniques.instrument: as ct_midsagittal_apd: CT workstation, bone window, 4.00x display, cursor in mm
techniques.how: Canal transverse diameter (TD): on the axial cut at the point of maximum pedicle width, the distance between the inner (medial) borders of the two pedicles, an interpedicular distance, at L1 to L5. Fig. 2 also labels a VTD line across the vertebral body that the text never defines or reports.
Shape of the canal noted at each vertebral level as oval or trefoil, by eye; no criterion separating the two is given; proportions at L3 given only in words

within_paper: One cohort only: every value of this paper's own is from the same 120 abdominal CT scans (66 women, 54 men), each measured at L1 to L5 by all three techniques on the hospital CT workstation (APD and VAPD on the mid-sagittal cut, TD and shape on the axial cut), p. 71 (PDF 3). Tables 1 and 2 are the same subjects as Tables 3 and 4: Inference from the printed totals, each sex's Total in Table 1 or 2 is the sum of its five level Totals in Table 3 or 4 divided by 5 (e.g. female APD 5259.8 / 5 = 1051.96), so Tables 1 and 2 hold each subject's mean over L1 to L5, p. 73-74 (PDF 5-6). The 600 measurements of the stenosis counts are the 120 x 5 level values of Table 3, p. 74 (PDF 6).
